full_name: Entry visa required for this nationality
definition: Whether a national of the origin country needs a visa (as opposed to visa-free or visa-on-arrival entry) to enter for study.
notes: NP/IN/BD nationals need a visa for all ten destinations; matters for VN/PH/TH/LK origins (e.g. MY visa-free for some ASEAN passports, TH for PH).

possible_values: e.g. Form 157A (AU online in ImmiAccount) / IMM 1294 (CA) / DS-160 + I-20 (US) / INZ 1012 / VIDEX national visa (DE) / AVATS (IE) / EMGS online (MY)
definition: The official form or portal form the student completes.
notes: Useful for checklist views; form codes change rarely.

definition: How the application is lodged: ImmiAccount (AU), IRCC secure account (CA), UKVI online then VFS biometrics (GB), INZ online (NZ), CEAC DS-160 then consular interview (US), VIDEX then embassy appointment (DE), AVATS then VFS (IE), EMGS portal via institution (MY), university lodges with ICP/GDRFA (AE), Thai e-Visa (TH).
notes: Nationality axis because some embassies outsource to VFS only in certain origins.

possible_values: e.g. VFS Global Kathmandu (Naxal) for GB/CA/AU biometrics; IOM Kathmandu (health); US Embassy Maharajgunj; VFS Delhi/Mumbai/Kolkata; VFS Dhaka
definition: Physical centres in the origin country where the applicant gives biometrics, submits passports or attends interview for this destination.
notes: Store address + booking URL. Nepal has no DE embassy VAC for all steps: DE national visa appointments at German Embassy Kathmandu via VIDEX.

full_name: Who may lodge or advise on the visa
possible_values: e.g. AU: only registered migration agents (MARA), legal practitioners or exempt persons may give immigration assistance; education agents may only do clerical lodging under the student's ImmiAccount; CA: paid representatives must be RCIC/lawyer (IMM 5476); UK: OISC-regulated; US: no regulation but agent cannot attend interview
definition: The legal rule on whether an education agency may prepare or lodge the visa and what disclaimer must accompany advice.
notes: Drives the MARN/general-information disclaimer in every visa answer. Owner is compliance.

possible_values: required / not_required / unknown (store as allowed / not_allowed / conditional)
definition: Whether a student already in the destination on another visa can lodge the student visa from inside the country.
notes: AU yes unless condition 8503/8534/8535; UK yes except from Visitor/short-term; CA generally no from visitor status since 28 Aug 2024 (limited exceptions); US change of status possible but travel-locked; NZ yes; DE yes if entered on a visa that permits it; MY/AE via institution. See E.107 (onshore_switching_rules) for the visitor-to-student case.

full_name: Bridging / interim status while onshore application is decided
possible_values: e.g. AU Bridging Visa A granted automatically with work rights of the substantive visa; CA implied (maintained) status if applied before expiry; UK 3C leave; US pending change-of-status; NZ interim visa
definition: What status the applicant holds between lodging onshore and decision, and whether work and study continue.
notes: Interacts with course-progress rules in academic-rules.md.

possible_values: e.g. UK 6 months (offshore) / 3 months (onshore); US I-20 issued up to 365 days ahead, visa up to 365 days ahead (entry within 30 days); CA no limit once LOA + PAL issued; AU no formal limit (CoE-driven); NZ no limit
definition: How early a student may lodge relative to the course start date.
notes: Store as {value, unit, months}. Pairs with recommended lodge-by dates in intake-calendar.md.

possible_values: e.g. US no earlier than 30 days before I-20 start; UK up to 1 month before if course over 6 months (1 week if shorter); AU any time after grant before course start; CA any time before permit expiry; DE within visa validity then register
definition: The earliest and latest dates the student may enter relative to course start.
notes: Latest-arrival is also an institution rule (intake-calendar.md latest arrival date).

possible_values: e.g. AU course end + 2 months (+ 3 or 4 months if course over 10 months ending Nov-Dec); UK course + 4 months (degree 12+ months) / + 2 months (6-12 months) / + 7 days; CA course + 90 days; US duration of status (D/S) + 60 days; NZ up to 4 years then renew; DE 1-2 years renewable; IE 1 year Stamp 2 renewable; MY 12 months renewable; AE 1 year renewable; TH 90 days then annual extension
definition: The formula the destination uses to set the visa expiry relative to the course.
notes: Feeds the post-study window in post-study-migration.md.

full_name: Physical / digital evidence of the visa
possible_values: evisa_only / vignette_then_evisa / brp_card / visa_sticker / i20_plus_stamp / residence_card / passport_sticker_plus_card
definition: What the student receives as proof of the visa (AU electronic only with VEVO; UK entry vignette then eVisa/UKVI account since BRP phase-out; CA port-of-entry letter then permit printed at border; US visa foil + I-20 + I-94; DE visa sticker then Aufenthaltstitel card; IE visa sticker then IRP card; MY single-entry visa then Student Pass sticker + i-Kad; AE entry permit then residence visa + Emirates ID; TH sticker).
notes: Pre-departure checklists (accommodation-arrival.md) reference this.

possible_values: e.g. US F-1: NP 60 months multiple entry; IN 60 months; BD 60 months; VN 12 months
definition: For destinations where the entry visa (foil) has a nationality-based reciprocity validity distinct from the permitted stay.
notes: US reciprocity schedule on travel.state.gov; matters for travel home mid-course.

possible_values: e.g. US needs valid visa foil + I-20 travel signature (within 12 months); CA needs valid TRV or eTA and permit; AU multiple entry within grant; UK multiple entry; TH re-entry permit THB 1,000 single / 3,800 multiple; DE card + passport; MY multiple-entry once Student Pass endorsed
definition: Whether the student can leave and return during study and what documents re-entry requires.
notes: Dashain/Tihar/Eid travel questions route here.

full_name: Grace period after course end or visa expiry
possible_values: e.g. US 60 (F-1 after program end) / 15 (after authorised withdrawal); CA 90 (restoration window); UK 0 (leave by expiry); AU 0 (grant already includes buffer); NZ 0
definition: Days the student may lawfully remain after the visa or program end before becoming unlawful, or the window in which status can be restored.
notes: Do not confuse with E.013 buffer built into grant length.

possible_values: e.g. CA restoration within 90 days (fee CAD 239 + new permit fee, cannot study meanwhile); US reinstatement via I-539 within 5 months of SEVIS termination; AU Bridging Visa E then new application onshore (s48 bar may apply); UK none, overstayer must leave
definition: What a student can do if the visa lapses or is cancelled.
notes: Always paired with MARN referral.

full_name: Extending or renewing to finish study
possible_values: e.g. AU new 500 application onshore with new CoE and GS; UK extend online (academic progression rule); CA extend study permit online before expiry; US I-20 program extension by DSO before end date; DE Aufenthaltstitel renewal at Ausländerbehörde; IE renew IRP annually; MY renew Student Pass via EMGS 2-3 months before expiry
definition: How a student extends the visa when the course runs longer or they progress to a further course.
notes: Ties to academic-rules.md leave-of-absence impact.

full_name: Visa rule for standalone English (ELICOS / pre-sessional)
possible_values: e.g. AU 500 ELICOS sector, no English test needed, GS still applies; UK Short-term study (6-11 months English) or Student visa if part of a package; CA study permit needed if over 6 months; US F-1 for intensive English programs; DE language-course visa (s16f) not convertible in all cases
definition: Whether and how a student can obtain a visa for an English-only course and whether it packages with the main course.
notes: Level axis value pathway_english. Packaging detail in pathways-articulation.md.

possible_values: e.g. UK Standard Visitor (up to 6 months study) / Short-term study visa (English 6-11 months); CA no permit needed under 6 months; AU 600 visitor for under 3 months; US B-2 limited / F-1; IE Stamp 2A; NZ visitor visa up to 3 months study
definition: Which visa covers courses too short for the main student visa.
notes: Alternatives (S17) for students who fail main-visa funds.

possible_values: e.g. IE register with ISD/Garda for IRP within 90 days; DE Anmeldung at Bürgeramt within 14 days then Aufenthaltstitel at Ausländerbehörde before visa expiry; MY EMGS medical within 7 days and Student Pass endorsement; AE medical fitness + Emirates ID + residence stamping within 60 days; UK collect BRP / create UKVI account, register with police no longer required; AU notify address within 7 days (8533); US SEVIS registration by DSO within 30 days
definition: The steps and deadlines the student must complete after arrival to hold lawful status.
notes: accommodation-arrival.md owns the how-to (tax ID, address); this row owns the immigration obligation and deadline.

possible_values: e.g. TH 90-day report to Immigration (TM47) / online; MY none beyond renewal; DE report address change; AU 8533 address change within 7 days; US report address change to DSO within 10 days; UK report change of address / circumstances via UKVI
definition: Recurring immigration reporting the visa holder must do while in the country.
notes: TH 90-day reporting is the reason for this row.

full_name: How the visa fee is paid
possible_values: e.g. credit/debit card in ImmiAccount (AU, surcharge applies) / IRCC online / UKVI online / bank draft or cash at embassy in local currency (DE Kathmandu) / EMGS invoice via institution (MY) / US MRV fee at designated bank (Nepal: Nabil)
definition: Accepted payment channels and any currency or local-bank rule in the origin market.
notes: Nepal-specific: NRB foreign-exchange rules covered in application-process.md.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. AUD 2,000 (AU 2026) / CAD 150 / GBP 524 / NZD 850 / USD 185 (F-1 MRV) + SEVIS
definition: Government charge for lodging the primary student visa application, before biometrics, medical or priority fees.
notes: Onshore vs offshore lodgement can differ (AU subsequent-entrant/onshore surcharges). Quote with the date checked; fees move annually (AU 1 July, GB spring, US as announced).

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} per adult / per child
definition: Government charge per accompanying spouse or child, whether lodged together with the student or as a subsequent entrant.
notes: Some destinations charge per person (AU, GB IHS per dependant), others one combined application (US dependants file DS-160 each). Money detail for families is `P.additional_funds_per_dependant`.

definition: Whether fingerprints and photo must be captured at a visa application centre or embassy before the decision.
notes: Required for NP/IN/BD applicants in CA, GB, US (interview) and AU (most VAC cities); exemptions for some ASEAN passports in MY/TH.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. CAD 85 / GBP 19.20 / AUD included
definition: Charge for the biometric collection appointment, separate from the visa fee.
notes: Some VACs add a service fee on top; record the government charge here and VAC service fees in notes.

definition: Typical days between requesting a biometrics slot and the earliest available appointment in the origin country.
notes: Counsellor-observed; spikes before major intakes (Jun–Jul, Dec–Jan). Never quoted as a guarantee.

definition: Whether a pre-lodgement or on-request immigration medical (chest X-ray, general exam, blood tests) is required for this nationality and course length.
notes: AU: required for most NP/IN/BD/VN/PH applicants (TB risk) via HAP ID; CA: IME for stays over 6 months from listed countries; GB: TB certificate only; US: none for F-1; NZ: chest X-ray + medical over 6/12 months.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. NPR 7,000–12,000 at IOM Kathmandu
definition: What the panel clinic charges in the origin country for the required medical, per applicant.
notes: Origin-country fee; children and X-ray-only cases cost less. Source: panel clinic price lists.

definition: Typical days from booking to results being transmitted to the immigration authority (eMedical / IME) in the origin country.
notes: Observed by branches; IOM Kathmandu backlog before Feb/Jul intakes is common.

full_name: Approved panel clinics by origin country
definition: The immigration authority's approved medical clinics in the student's home country for this destination.
notes: AU/CA/NZ/GB publish panel lists; US embassy lists panel physicians for immigrant visas only (F-1 needs none).

full_name: TB test required for these origin countries
possible_values: ISO-2 origin list e.g. [NP, IN, BD, VN, PH, LK, TH]
definition: Origin countries whose nationals (or long-term residents) must present a tuberculosis clearance for a study visa longer than the threshold stay.
notes: GB: TB certificate from an approved clinic for stays over 6 months; AU/NZ/CA fold TB screening into the medical. A residency test applies, not just nationality.

full_name: Visa fee refund on refusal or withdrawal
possible_values: e.g. non-refundable (AU, GB, US) / refundable if withdrawn before processing (CA)
definition: Whether the government visa charge is refunded on refusal, withdrawal or duplicate lodgement.
notes: Distinct from the institution refund on visa refusal (`L.visa_refusal_refund_pct`).

possible_values: required / not_required / unknown (store as available / not_available / conditional)
definition: Whether a paid or eligibility-based faster processing stream exists for student visas, and who qualifies.
notes: CA SDS/PAL streams (see E.050); GB priority and super-priority services for a fee; AU none (ministerial direction ordering); US expedited interview requests case-by-case.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. GBP 500 priority / GBP 1,000 super priority
definition: Cost of the expedited processing stream where one exists.
notes: Only where E.036 is available.

possible_values: e.g. {amount: 29710, currency: AUD, period: per_year, year: 2025}
definition: Funds the student must show for the visa (GIC / blocked account / bank balance).
notes: Seed row (definition verbatim; seed type `object` {amount, currency} normalised to money). This is the headline total the formula in E.039 produces for a single offshore applicant; components are E.040–E.046. All ten destinations require some funds evidence for NP/IN/BD nationals; AU may waive documentary evidence for low-risk provider/nationality combinations (E.047).

possible_values: e.g. AU: 12 months living (AUD 29,710) + first-year tuition − prepaid + travel; CA: tuition + GIC/living CAD 20,635 + travel; GB: 9 months maintenance + first-year tuition − paid
definition: The published formula the immigration authority uses to compute the minimum funds a student must evidence, expressed in its own components.
notes: Each component is catalogued separately (E.040–E.046); this row is the assembled rule the financial-proof calculator (07 view 3) displays.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: per_year | per_month, year} e.g. AUD 29,710/yr; GBP 1,483/month London, 1,136 outside; CAD 20,635/yr
definition: The immigration authority's own living-cost amount for the student, used in the funds formula (not the institution's or a city estimate).
notes: Region axis for GB (London vs rest) and CA (Quebec has its own figure). City-level realistic costs are `D.*`; this is the legal minimum.

full_name: Official living-cost figure — spouse or partner
possible_values: {amount, currency, period, year} e.g. AUD 10,394/yr; GBP 845/month London
definition: Additional funds the authority requires for an accompanying partner.
notes: Family total is computed in `P.additional_funds_per_dependant`.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period, year} e.g. AUD 4,449/yr per child + school costs
definition: Additional funds the authority requires per accompanying child, excluding school fees.
notes: School fees are `E.044` and `P.public_school_fee_by_region`.

full_name: Tuition component of the funds formula
possible_values: e.g. first 12 months of tuition less amount already paid (AU/GB); first year (CA); full program I-20 estimate (US)
definition: How much tuition must be evidenced and whether prepaid tuition is deducted.
notes: US I-20 shows the school's full first-year estimate incl. living; the consular officer applies it as the benchmark.

possible_values: e.g. AU: AUD 13,502/yr per school-age child unless exempt; GB: none in formula; CA: none
definition: Whether and how children's schooling costs enter the funds formula.
notes: Fee exemptions by state/province are `P.school_fee_exemptions`.

full_name: Travel component of the funds formula
possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off} e.g. AUD 2,500 (from Nepal/India), AUD 3,000 elsewhere
definition: Return travel allowance the authority adds to the funds requirement, if any.
notes: AU publishes region-based travel amounts; CA adds transport; GB/US have no separate travel line.

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: per_month, months: 9} e.g. GBP 1,483 London / GBP 1,136 outside London
definition: Destination-specific maintenance requirement where the official figure varies by where the student will study.
notes: GB Student route; CA Quebec vs other provinces. Elsewhere identical to E.040.

full_name: Financial evidence level by provider risk rating
definition: Whether documentary evidence of funds must be attached at lodgement, driven by the provider's and the nationality's risk rating (AU evidence levels 1–3).
notes: AU publishes neither provider nor country levels; Expert observes them per partner. Internal: use to advise, never quote a level to a student.

possible_values: e.g. 28 days (GB) / 90 days (AU practice) / 3 months (CA GIC alternative)
definition: Minimum number of consecutive days the required balance must have been held before the statement date.
notes: GB: 28-day rule is statutory; AU: no statute but recent large deposits trigger genuine-source scrutiny (see E.058).

possible_values: e.g. 31 days (GB) / 3 months (AU, CA) / 6 months (US practice)
definition: How recent bank statements or certificates must be at the time of lodgement or interview.
notes: Counts from statement date to lodgement date (GB) or interview date (US).

full_name: SDS / PAL and other streamlined-processing variants
definition: Which processing variant applies to this nationality: legacy Student Direct Stream (closed Nov 2024), Provincial Attestation Letter requirement, or trusted-institution framework.
notes: PAL/TAL required for most CA study permits since 2024 caps; DLI issues it after acceptance and provincial allocation (`W.caps_policy`).

definition: Guaranteed Investment Certificate amount required for the study permit (budget planning).
notes: Seed row (definition verbatim). Quebec figure differs; GIC is one accepted evidence route, not mandatory outside the former SDS. Providers are `L.finance_provider_name`.

definition: Amount that must be deposited in a Sperrkonto (or equivalent) before the German national visa is granted, released monthly to the student.
notes: Set by BAföG rate; changes each academic year. Providers are `L.finance_provider_name`.

possible_values: e.g. AU: partner AUD 10,394 + child AUD 4,449 + school fees; GB: GBP 845/680 per dependant per month for 9 months
definition: How the funds formula grows for each accompanying family member.
notes: Computed family amounts and eligibility are domain P; this is the visa-side rule text.

possible_values: required / not_required / unknown (store as accepted / not_accepted)
definition: Whether a sponsor's or student's annual income can replace lump-sum savings as financial evidence.
notes: AU accepts personal or parent/spouse income above E.055/E.056 with official tax evidence; other destinations require balances.

definition: Minimum gross annual income of the student, parent or spouse that satisfies the income alternative for an unaccompanied student.
notes: Evidence: official tax assessment for the most recent year.

definition: Minimum gross annual income that satisfies the income alternative when family members accompany the student.
notes: Only the higher threshold applies once any dependant is included.

possible_values: savings / fixed_deposit / education_loan / gic / blocked_account / scholarship_letter / sponsor_income / property_sale_proceeds
definition: Categories of money the authority accepts as evidence, in its own terms.
notes: Fixed deposits must be liquid or loan-backed for AU; CA counts GIC, bank drafts, loans, scholarships; US accepts any liquid funds with a bank letter.

possible_values: e.g. AU: recent large deposits must be traceable to a documented source (sale deed, gift declaration)
definition: Whether and how the origin of recently deposited funds must be explained and evidenced.
notes: The single most common Nepal/Bangladesh refusal ground; pairs with E.048 seasoning.

possible_values: land_and_buildings_valuation / gold / vehicles / shares / business_valuation / none
definition: Non-cash assets the authority will count, if any, and how they must be valued.
notes: Most destinations count assets only as loan collateral or income evidence, not as available funds; US officers may weigh them qualitatively.

possible_values: tax_certificate / salary_slips / audited_accounts / rental_agreements / pension_statement / agricultural_income_certificate
definition: Documents the authority accepts to prove regular income of the student or sponsor.
notes: Nepal: tax clearance from IRD, ward office income verification; India: ITR-V; Bangladesh: NBR tax return.

possible_values: self / parent / spouse / sibling / grandparent / uncle_aunt / in_law / unrelated_third_party / employer / government
definition: Who may fund the student for the funds to count, as the authority defines it.
notes: GB: only parents, legal guardians or the student (and partner) unless via an official sponsor; AU: any relationship with a declared reason; US: any sponsor with affidavit of support (I-134 not required for F-1 but often used).

definition: Limit on how many people may jointly fund the application.
notes: Practice more than statute; multiple unrelated sponsors are a credibility red flag everywhere.

possible_values: e.g. AU: sanction letter + disbursement capability; CA: loan from a Canadian or recognised bank; GB: loan letter dated within 6 months from a regulated institution
definition: Conditions under which an education loan counts as available funds (sanction vs disbursement, lender type, collateral).
notes: Nepali bank sanction letters are accepted by AU/CA/US when the bank is a licensed A-class bank; loan products are the L loan rows (`L.loan_lender_type` onwards).

full_name: Currency and translation rules for financial documents
possible_values: e.g. statements in NPR accepted with certified English translation; conversion at the authority's rate on lodgement date
definition: How foreign-currency statements are converted and whether certified translations are needed.
notes: Attestation norms for all documents are E.116; FX conventions for displaying converted figures are `V.fx_rate_used`/`V.fx_as_of`.

definition: The concrete list of financial documents to attach for this nationality and level, assembled from E.057–E.064.
notes: Feeds the document checklist view (07 view 12) with the money section.

definition: Whether the immigration authority itself (not the institution) requires evidence of English for the student visa.
notes: AU: required unless exempt (see E.069); GB: B2 via SELT or degree-level sponsor assessment; CA/US/NZ: no visa-side test, institution decides; DE: language of instruction proof.

possible_values: e.g. IELTS Academic/General, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, CAE, OET (AU); SELT list (GB)
definition: Which tests, and which editions (home/online), the authority accepts for the visa-side requirement.
notes: Institution acceptance is `I.english_test_accepted`; test catalog is domain I. TOEFL iBT Home Edition and IELTS Online are not accepted for AU visas.

possible_values: {test, overall, min_band} e.g. AU IELTS 6.0 overall (5.5 with 10-week ELICOS; 5.0 with 20 weeks); GB CEFR B2 for degree level, B1 below
definition: Minimum score the authority requires, per test, for this level, including packaged-English variants.
notes: Equivalence across tests is `I.english_equivalence_table`.

definition: Grounds on which the visa-side English test is waived.
notes: AU: 2+ years study in English in the last 2 years; GB: majority-English-speaking countries and UK degrees. Institution waivers are `I.moi_waiver_levels_accepted`.

possible_values: e.g. AU: taken within 2 years of lodgement; GB: SELT within 2 years
definition: How old the test may be at lodgement for the visa purpose.
notes: Admission-side validity is `I.visa_english_validity_months` / `I.test_validity_months`.

full_name: Genuine-intent test name and legal basis
possible_values: Genuine Student (GS) requirement (AU, from 23 Mar 2024) / bona fide student & intent (CA) / genuine student & credibility (GB) / non-immigrant intent 214(b) (US) / bona fide (NZ)
definition: The destination's test of whether the applicant is a genuine temporary student, as named in law or policy.
notes: Replaces AU GTE. The test drives the SOP/GS-statement framing counsellors help students write.

possible_values: e.g. AU GS: circumstances in home country; value of the course; circumstances in Australia; immigration history; compliance history; other relevant matters
definition: The factors the officer must weigh, in the authority's own wording, for this test.
notes: Order matters for the SOP structure. US: ties to home country, funding, study plan credibility.

full_name: Genuine-intent statement word limits and questions
possible_values: [{question, word_limit}] e.g. AU GS: 4 targeted questions, 150 words each
definition: The exact questions and length limits of the genuine-intent statement in the application form.
notes: AU GS questions replaced the free-form GTE statement in 2024. US has no written statement (interview only).

full_name: Package / pathway assessment rule for genuine intent
possible_values: e.g. AU: assessed against the principal course; ELICOS + diploma + degree packages need a coherent progression narrative
definition: How a packaged offer (English + pathway + degree) is assessed under the genuine-intent test.
notes: Packaging mechanics are `J.single_visa_packaging`.

full_name: Study-gap and age scrutiny under genuine intent
possible_values: e.g. gaps over 2 years and applicants over 30 for bachelor level attract closer scrutiny; explain with employment evidence
definition: How study gaps, age relative to level and career changes are weighed in the genuine-intent assessment.
notes: Observed decision pattern, not a published rule; use to advise on evidence, never quote thresholds as law. Gap tolerance for admission is `A.study_gap_max_years`.

definition: Whether the authority interviews applicants of this nationality and level (mandatory consular interview vs risk-triggered call).
notes: US: always (consular); GB: credibility interviews common for NP/IN/BD; AU/CA: telephone verification on risk triggers; NZ/DE/IE: rare. Course-level admissions interviews are `A.interview_required`.

definition: How the visa interview, if any, is conducted for applicants from this origin.
notes: US F-1 interviews at the embassy in the origin country (Kathmandu, New Delhi, Dhaka); GB video credibility interviews via UKVI.

possible_values: e.g. prior refusal; course unrelated to background; sponsor unrelated; recent large deposit; agent history
definition: Circumstances observed to trigger a credibility or verification interview.
notes: Expert-observed; feeds the risk panel (07 view 8). Never quoted.

definition: Typical processing time for the destination student visa.
notes: Seed row (definition verbatim; decimal weeks, indicative). Official published range is E.080; branch-observed times are E.081/E.082 and internal.

possible_values: {p50_days, p90_days, as_of} e.g. AU: 50% in 21 days, 90% in 6 weeks
definition: The authority's published processing statistics for the student visa (median and 90th percentile where given).
notes: AU global visa processing times page; CA per-country processing tool; GB 3-week standard; US appointment wait tracker.

full_name: Observed processing time from this origin
definition: What Expert's branches actually observe for applicants from this origin country, from lodgement to decision.
notes: Internal only; often longer than the official figure for NP/BD. Quote the official range to students.

definition: Date of the most recent observation batch behind E.081.
notes: Staleness beyond 60 days should hide E.081 from reasoning.

definition: Share of finalised student-visa applications granted for this nationality (and sector or level where published).
notes: AU publishes by citizenship and sector; CA publishes approval rates by country; GB/US publish issuance counts (rate derived). Quote with period.

possible_values: e.g. FY2024-25 / calendar 2025 / rolling 12 months to Jun 2026
definition: The period the published grant rate covers.
notes: Always shown next to E.083.

possible_values: e.g. lodge before May for July intake; December shutdowns add 2–3 weeks
definition: Practical timing guidance around intake peaks and public-holiday slowdowns.
notes: Feeds the backward timeline (07 view 5) as buffer weeks.

possible_values: e.g. US: enter up to 30 days before I-20 start; AU: no earlier-entry limit, must arrive before course start; CA: before study start, at officer's discretion
definition: Rules on how early the student may lodge and how early or late they may enter the country relative to course start.
notes: Earliest lodgement is E.011/E.012; this row is the travel window.

possible_values: [{code, title, summary, breach_consequence}] e.g. AU 8105 work limit, 8202 enrolment/attendance, 8501 health insurance, 8533 address notification, 8534 no further stay; US F-1 status rules (8 CFR 214.2(f)); CA study permit conditions
definition: The enforceable conditions printed on or implied by the student visa, each with its code (where the destination uses codes) and the consequence of breach.
notes: Institution-side operationalisation (attendance %, progress) is domain O; this row is the legal condition.

definition: Permitted work hours during study on the student visa.
notes: Seed row (definition verbatim). Convention: store the term-time weekly cap (AU 48 per fortnight → 24; CA 24; GB 20 degree / 10 below; US 20 on-campus only; NZ 20; DE 140 full days or 280 half days per year → note; IE 20; MY 20 during breaks only; AE by permit; TH none). Break-time rule is E.090; the seed's 'unlimited in breaks' convention is handled there, so this integer is always the term-time cap.

possible_values: e.g. AU 48 hours per fortnight while the course is in session; GB 20 hours per week (10 for below-degree); US on-campus 20 hours, off-campus only via CPT/OPT/severe economic hardship; CA 24 hours per week off-campus if eligible; MY 20 hours only during breaks of 7+ days
definition: The full term-time work rule in the authority's wording, including the counting period (week vs fortnight), on/off-campus distinction and eligibility preconditions.
notes: E.088 holds the normalised integer; this row keeps the nuance (fortnight counting, on-campus only, master's-by-research unlimited).

possible_values: e.g. AU unlimited during scheduled course breaks; CA full-time during scheduled breaks; GB full-time in vacations; US on-campus full-time during breaks, off-campus needs authorisation; NZ full-time in scheduled holidays (and Dec–Jan for degree students)
definition: Hours permitted during official semester breaks and between courses.

possible_values: e.g. AU: only once the course has commenced; CA: once studies begin and permit says so; GB: from the visa start date; US: on-campus up to 30 days before program start, off-campus after one academic year (CPT) or on completion (OPT)
definition: The earliest point at which the student may lawfully begin working after arrival.

full_name: Placements and internships count toward the work cap
possible_values: required / not_required / unknown (store as counts / exempt / conditional)
definition: Whether a mandatory course placement, internship or work-integrated-learning component counts against the permitted work hours.

full_name: Self-employment, gig and business activity rules
possible_values: e.g. GB: no self-employment, no business activity, no professional sportsperson; AU: self-employment allowed within hours cap (ABN work counts); CA: self-employment counts as work within 24 hours; US: prohibited without authorisation
definition: Whether the student may drive for ride-share, freelance, run a business or hold an ABN/sole-trader registration, and how such hours are counted.
notes: Frequent Uber/Doordash question; ride-share is self-employment in GB (prohibited) but permitted in AU within the cap.

definition: Whether the student visa permits bringing dependents for this course/level.
notes: Seed row (definition verbatim). The one canonical dependants-by-level row; GB since Jan 2024 only postgraduate research and government-sponsored; CA since 2024 only master's/doctoral and some professional degrees for spousal open work permits; AU all levels but funds and genuine-intent scrutiny apply. Who counts, their rights and money are domain P.

possible_values: e.g. AU: must maintain enrolment in a registered full-time course (8202); US: full course of study each term (12 credits UG / 9 PG), one online class max counted; CA: actively pursuing studies; GB: sponsor-defined full time
definition: The visa-side obligation to stay enrolled full-time and how 'full-time' is defined for immigration purposes.
notes: Reduced-load permissions are `O.reduced_load_visa_impact`; this row is the condition itself.

possible_values: e.g. AU 8533: notify provider of address within 7 days of arrival and of any change within 7 days; US: SEVIS address update within 10 days; GB: update UKVI account; CA: keep IRCC informed
definition: What the student must report to the authority or the institution and within how many days.

full_name: Age limits for the student visa
possible_values: {min_age, max_age, notes} e.g. AU: min 6 for schooling, no max; GB Child Student 4–17, Student 16+; CA minors need custodian; DE none

possible_values: e.g. AU: cancellation under s116, possible 3-year exclusion (PIC 4013/4014); US: termination of SEVIS record, unlawful presence; GB: curtailment; CA: removal order and future inadmissibility

possible_values: [{ground, legal_basis, share_pct, period}] e.g. AU: genuine student (cl 500.212), financial capacity (500.214), English (500.213), PIC 4020 fraud; US: 214(b) non-immigrant intent
definition: Why student visas from this origin are refused, with the legal basis and, where published, the share of refusals each ground accounts for.

possible_values: e.g. AU: decision record PDF in ImmiAccount with reasons and review rights; CA: refusal letter with tick-box reasons, GCMS notes obtainable via ATIP; GB: refusal notice with paragraphs cited; US: 214(b) letter with no detailed reasons

possible_values: e.g. AU Administrative Review Tribunal (onshore applicants only, offshore need a sponsor); CA Federal Court judicial review (leave required); GB administrative review; US none (re-apply only); NZ Immigration and Protection Tribunal (limited)

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. AUD 3,496 (ART, 2025); GBP 80 administrative review; CAD 50 Federal Court filing
definition: Government fee for lodging the review or appeal.

possible_values: e.g. 21 or 28 days (AU depending on notification method) / 15 days from refusal (CA leave) / 14 days (GB)

possible_values: e.g. no bar on re-applying but must address the reasons; AU offshore can re-lodge immediately with a new CoE; GB must not repeat the same evidence; US new DS-160 and fee, interview again; CA re-apply after obtaining GCMS notes

possible_values: e.g. AU PIC 4020: 3-year bar for bogus documents or false information, 10 years for identity fraud; CA misrepresentation 5-year inadmissibility (A40); GB 10-year ban for deception; US 212(a)(6)(C)(i) permanent inadmissibility

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: one_off, year} e.g. AUD 2,000 adult + AUD 500 child (AU 2026)
definition: Government charge for a dependant who applies after the student's grant, where it differs from the combined-application fee.

possible_values: e.g. AU subsequent entrant: often 3–6 months, longer than primary; CA SOWP: 8–12 weeks; US F-2: consular appointment wait
definition: Typical time for a dependant application, especially when lodged separately.

possible_values: [{member: partner|child, amount, currency, period, year, notes}] e.g. AU: partner AUD 10,394, child AUD 4,449 + school fees AUD 13,502; GB: partner/child GBP 845 pm London, GBP 680 outside, × 9 months

full_name: Public school fees for dependant children
possible_values: {amount, currency, period: per_year, year} e.g. NSW AUD 6,900 primary / 8,500 secondary (2025, temporary residents); VIC AUD 13,502 unless exempt; QLD ~AUD 12,000; CA/GB/US free

possible_values: {start_age, end_age} e.g. NSW 6–17; VIC 6–17; ON 6–18; England 5–16 (18 in education or training)

possible_values: {typical_daily_cost, currency, subsidy_eligible: tristate, scheme} e.g. AU: AUD 130–180/day, Child Care Subsidy not available to most student-visa holders; GB: 15/30 free hours not available to most visa holders; CA: provincial subsidies vary

possible_values: {amount, currency, period: per_week|per_month, year} e.g. Melbourne 2-bed unit AUD 550–700/week (2025)

full_name: Tax and benefits position of a working partner

full_name: Status of a child born in the destination
possible_values: e.g. AU: child takes the parents' visa status (added to the student visa, must be notified); CA and US: birthright citizenship; GB: no automatic citizenship, child must be added to leave

full_name: Citizenship for children born in the destination

possible_values: [{document, weight, notes}] e.g. marriage certificate (registered), joint photos across time, joint bank account or remittances, chat logs, statutory declarations, de facto: 12 months cohabitation evidence

full_name: English requirement for dependants — visa side

possible_values: {min_years, standard_years, max_years} e.g. AU PhD 3–4; GB 3–4; US 5–6; DE 3–5

possible_values: e.g. AU 485: 3 years for doctorate (from 2024); GB Graduate route 3 years for PhD; CA PGWP up to 3 years; DE 18-month job-seeker

full_name: Migration points advantage for a doctorate
possible_values: e.g. AU: 20 points for a doctorate (vs 15 bachelor/master's) plus 10 for STEM research master's/PhD specialist qualification
